This prediction was primarily influenced by a few key aspects of your academic profile.

Your performance in Year 3 of your studies was a significant factor. This suggests that your academic performance in that year was a concern for the model, as it indicated a potential struggle with the rigorous demands of law school.

On a more positive note, your LSAT score and undergraduate GPA were both strengths in your application. Your LSAT score, while slightly below the average of 37.27 for successful students, still contributed positively by suggesting a reasonable aptitude for legal studies. Similarly, your undergraduate GPA of 3.40 was above the average of 3.24, indicating a solid academic foundation.

Despite these strengths, the model placed considerable weight on your Year 3 academic performance, which ultimately tipped the balance toward a prediction of bar exam failure. This was the most influential factor, overshadowing the positive contributions of your LSAT score and GPA.

Moving forward, consider focusing on improving any areas of academic weakness and perhaps gaining additional experience or credentials that could strengthen your future applications. This might involve retaking certain courses or seeking opportunities to demonstrate your capabilities in a legal context. By addressing these areas, you can enhance your profile and increase your chances of success in future applications.
